Name: Marsha Tyson
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I am a science teacher and love that you use the language inquiry cycle. We talk in terms of inquiry all the time in science. We ask questions, make connections, gather data, analyze data, refine our questions and use the evidence in our explanations. Questions drive the learning and this module did this for me. Sensemaking was happening after each text, just like new pieces of data.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
A meaningful moment is around the selection of texts. NWP did a great job of curating meaningful texts to accompany each topic. This was great that it was already curated. It has revealed to me I need to make sure to select my texts carefully with different topics. I wonder if AI can help me do this.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
I did this for a group of teachers, since I do not have my own class of students. It was really interesting to see how much additional writing was done after each round and how the final writing came together. They were using their resources and citing them too.
